43747943.article_content:
The Xilinx ISE Installer Lies
For various reasons, I wanted to run Xilinx ISE (predecessors to Vivado) in a parallel and portable manner (think of something like running place and route on thousands of digital designs for FPGAs). Now, ISE is no longer being developed, but they obviously keep some of the recent versions hosted for their gray-haired customers. They have a Linux installer, but it’s always a pain to set up, and it can be super annoying to get all the right dependencies and environment set up correctly, so I wanted to make a Docker image so I can do it portably and reproducibly. Cool, sounds like a reasonable idea.
I grabbed the installer for the very last version they ever released, which is a 6.1 GB tar file. Docker has to copy this file into the image every time for the build, which takes more than 30 seconds, which is annoying (I also know about bind mounts during build time, but let’s say I want to include the file with the image). If I also want to host the installer file along with the Dockerfile on GitHub as an asset for the build, I also need to split it into around 60 file chunks, each 90 MB. These issues are all caused by the large file size of the installer, which makes it the main problem to solve.
So I first tried to compress the installer with gzip, but it barely reduced the file size. So I looked into the tar file itself, and almost all the large install files are .zip.xz files. Okay, weird. Zip already supports compression inside the archive format, so why would they use xz to compress presumably uncompressed or compressed zip files? And also, why would they not just use zip with compression or tar and gzip for the installer as a whole?
I then decided to recompress these large .zip.xz files with a higher compression effort or a larger compression window using xz. I.e., I'm going to take all the xz files in the tar file, decompress them, recompress them with the highest compression effort, and put them back into the tar installer file, replacing the original xz files. This way, I can maybe reduce the overall tar file size and solve some of my issues, assuming that Xilinx did not compress these files with the highest effort already. (You would think they would care a lot about this issue since they have to serve this 6 GB installer file for download to users; i.e., the smaller they can make their installer, the more money they can save on bandwidth and network costs of these downloads) (I'm also making an educated guess that Xilinx doesn't care enough to do this).
Well, it turns out the ISE installer lies. These .zip.xz files are 7zip files, which are also password protected. Naturally, I found out what the password is (I won’t say it here, but there are several ways to find this out that are public). Now the new plan is to do the same recompression idea as before but recompress these 7zip files with the highest compression effort I can (using the delta filter + the supported lzma2 compression filter with the highest compression level).
I tried to do this on disk on my laptop by un-taring and un-7zipping the individual .zip.xz files into a temporary directory and then re-7zipping and recompressing them, and then reassembling the tar file with the new .zip.xz files. I ran out of disk space on my laptop (and there is I/O overhead). So then I decided to do this all in memory using Python since there are nice libraries for tar and 7zip, and I can selectively read out parts of the tar file and do everything in memory and possibly in parallel. I then crashed my laptop via OOM. I was able to print out some metrics while this ran, and I could see some files would only result in close to 0% file size reduction while some were closer to 6%. So it does work a little sometimes; I just haven’t run it all the way through to get the final overall file size reduction of the entire installer.
I'm still curious if I can make this work well. The recompression itself is also super slow, but I think the installer being 6 GB is so annoying that it’s a worthy issue for me to pester myself over. Previously, I was doing all this in Python with the py7zr library, but there is also a 7zip library in Rust that looks more promising, and I think there is a way to support zstd compression, but I’m not sure if the official 7zip tool supports zstd or whatever the Xilinx installer’s 7zip supports.
I guess the conclusion here is that Xilinx never ceases to "surprise" me with their software, not even with something as mundane as the installer.

data.title: Nerdlog: Fast, multi-host TUI log viewer with timeline histogram
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: Nerdlog是一个快速、多主机的TUI日志查看器，带有时间轴直方图，灵感来源于Graylog/Kibana，但更加轻量，几乎无需配置。该项目由一个需要处理大量分布式节点日志的团队开发，旨在替代缓慢的Splunk。Nerdlog通过SSH直接连接到各个节点，分析存储在节点本地的日志文件，无需集中式服务器。它支持从多个远程节点同时查询日志、按时间范围和模式过滤日志，并在终端界面中展示日志和直方图。日志分析在远程节点上进行，仅下载必要的数据，支持数据压缩以节省带宽。Nerdlog强调高效和便捷，适合习惯使用命令行的用户。项目代码托管在GitHub上。

Nerdlog: fast, multi-host TUI log viewer with timeline histogram
Loosely inspired by Graylog/Kibana, but without the bloat. Pretty much no setup needed, either.
Hosted on Github:
https://github.com/dimonomid/nerdlog
.
First of all, a little demo. Here, we're dealing with (fake) logs from 4 remote nodes, and simulating a scenario of drilling down into logs to find the issue, filtering out irrelevant messages and finding relevant ones.
Project history
It might be useful to know the history to understand the project motivation and overall direction.
My team and I were working on a service which was printing a fairly sizeable amount of logs from a distributed cluster of 20+ nodes: about 2-3M log messages per hour in total. There was no containerization: the nodes were actual AWS instances running Ubuntu, and our web services were running there directly as just systemd services, naturally printing logs to
/var/log/syslog
. To read the logs though, we were using Graylog, and querying those logs for an hour was taking no more than 1-3 seconds, so it was pretty quick.
Infra people hated Graylog though, since it required some annoying maintenance from them, and so at some point the decision was made to switch to Splunk instead. And when Splunk was finally rolled out, I had to find out that it was incredibly, ridiculously slow. Honestly, looking at it, I don't quite understand how they are even selling it. If you've used Splunk, you might know that it has two modes: “Smart” and “Fast”. In “Smart” mode, the same query for an hour of logs was taking _a few minutes_. And in so called “Fast” mode, it was taking 30-60s (and that “Fast” mode has some other limitations which makes it a lot less useful). It might have been a misconfiguration of some sort (I'm not an infra guy so I don't know), but no one knew how or wanted to fix it, and so it was clear that once Graylog is finally shut down, we'll lose our ability to query logs quickly, and it was a massive bummer for us.
And I thought that it's just ridiculous. 2-3M log messages doesn't sound like such a big amount of logs, and it seemed like some old-school shell hacks on plain log files, without having any centralized logging server, should be able to be about as fast as Graylog was, and it should be enough for most of our needs. As you remember, our stuff was running as systemd services printing logs to
/var/log/syslog
, so these plain log files were readily available to us.  And so that's how the project started: I couldn't stop thinking of it, so I took a week off, and went on a personal hackathon to implement this proof-of-concept log fetcher and viewer, which is ssh-ing directly to the nodes, and analyzing plain log files using
bash
+
tail
+
head
+
awk
hacks.
It has proven to be very capable of replacing the essential features we had in Graylog: being fast, querying logs from multiple remote nodes simultaneously, drawing the histogram for the whole requested time period, supporting context (key-value pairs) for every message. Apart from that, it was actually refreshing to use a snappy keyboard-navigated terminal app instead of clunky web UIs, so in a sense I liked it even more than Graylog. As to Splunk, I ended up almost never using it to fetch logs from our nodes.
So having that backstory, you can already get a feel of the goals and design of Nerdlog: it is laser-focused on being super efficient while querying logs from multiple remote machines simultaneously, filtering them by time range and patterns, and apart from showing the actual logs, also drawing the histogram.
Design highlights
No centralized server required; nerdlog establishes an ssh connection to every node that the user wants to collect logs from, and keeps them idle in the background (although a separate server to store the log files might still help in some cases; see the “Requirements” section below);
Logs are not downloaded to the local machine in full: all the log analysis is done on the remote nodes, and on each query, only the following data is downloaded from each node: up to 250 messages from every logstream (configurable), and data for the timeline histogram. It's obviously possible to paginate over the logs, to get the next bunch of messages, etc. Nerdlog then merges the responses from all nodes together, and presents to the user in a unified form;
Most of the data is gzipped in transit, thus saving the bandwidth as well.

data.title: Frankenstein's `__init__`
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了作者在Python生产代码中遇到的一个极为奇怪的`__init__`方法问题。作者试图为一个Python服务添加一个失败测试，但测试偶尔会因为`FooBarWidget`对象缺少`should_exit`属性而失败。经过调查，发现`FooBarWidget`继承自`FooWidget`，并在其`__init__`方法中启动了一个新线程来执行父类的`__init__`和`run`方法。这样做的目的是避免阻塞主线程，因为`zmq.Socket`不能在线程间移动。然而，这种实现导致了意外的错误和困惑，反映了在解决技术问题时对合理性和可维护性的忽视。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Python中构造器（`__init__`）的适当使用，特别是涉及外部资源（如zeromq socket）或复杂操作时的处理方式。

不同观点：
• [mjr00] 认为在`__init__`中进行复杂操作（如读取外部文件或创建zeromq socket）是不合理的。他主张遵循“最小惊讶原则”，建议将这些操作移到单独的连接/打开/关闭方法中，并通过contextmanager管理资源，以避免构造器失败的情况。

• [zokier] 提出可以通过多线程的方式解决这个问题，即在构造器中启动一个工作线程，并确保构造过程在构造器返回之前完成。这种方法虽然引入了多线程，但可以保证对象初始化的完整性。

• [wodenokoto] 对[mjr00]的评论表示部分赞同，但希望看到更人性化和合理的解决方案示例，而不仅仅是对问题的批评。

• [pjot] 则认为应该将所有对象初始化操作保留在主线程中，并将涉及zeromq socket的创建操作推迟到后台线程中执行，以保持代码的清晰性。

• [smitty1e] 引用Wheeler/Lampson的话，幽默地指出Python中的问题可以通过增加一层间接性来解决，暗示可以通过更复杂的结构来处理这些问题。

• [_Algernon_] 提出在`.close`方法中添加`time.sleep(0.1)`，虽然这个建议看似简单，但可能涉及到资源关闭时的时序问题。

补充讨论：
• [devrandoom] 对Python构造器的语法提出了一个简短的疑问，显示出对Python构造器语法的基本理解可能存在不确定性。

争议焦点：
• 在`__init__`中进行复杂操作是否合理，特别是当这些操作可能失败或涉及外部资源时。
• 如何平衡代码的简洁性与遵循最佳实践（如最小惊讶原则）之间的关系。
• 多线程解决方案是否合适，特别是在构造器中启动线程是否会增加代码的复杂性和潜在的错误风险。

Yep. You read that right: this class kicks off it’s parent’s
__init__
to a new thread
.
So if you
close
a
FooBarWidget
instance
too quickly
, you just might do it before
FooWidget.__init__
has finished,
resulting in pain, suffering, and a deep questioning of one’s life choices.
Why, Though?
Since you might be wondering why someone would even do this, first you need to know that a

To avoid blocking the main thread,

However, it cannot do so once

A solution, then: let both the
__init__
and the
run
execute in the new thread,
solving an annoying problem with a complete and utter disregard to sanity, common sense, and the feelings of other human beings.

I had desired it with an ardour that far exceeded moderation; but now that I had finished, the beauty of the dream vanished, and breathless horror and disgust filled my heart.
~
Frankenstein

data.title: Googler... ex-Googler
data.author: namukang
data.article_summary: 本文是一名谷歌员工Adam Argyle的告别帖，讲述他在谷歌的职位突然被取消，感到极度伤心和愤怒。尽管他被告知这不是基于个人表现，并可以寻找其他职位，但他立即被剥夺了对工作相关内容（如日历、文档和代码）的访问权限，感觉像被当作罪犯对待。他提到自己刚参加完团队建设活动，原本计划参与多个重要项目和会议，如Google IO，但这些机会全都瞬间消失。他感到被背叛和不被重视，多年建立的关系也可能就此终结。最后，他提供了新的联系方式，并表示需要时间消化这一变故。文章引发了大量同事的同情和支持。

不同观点：
• **裁员中的人性化处理**：

• **对公司情感投入的反思**：
  - [sudomateo] 强调员工与公司之间的关系是商业关系，员工不应将自己的价值完全与公司绑定。他们建议学会将自我价值与雇主区分开，以应对裁员带来的情感冲击。
  
• **对裁员的不满与失望**：
  - [azangru] 对Google裁掉一位他们非常尊敬的工程师感到失望，认为这反映了公司对开发者社区和卓越技术的承诺减弱。
  - [javawizard] 分享了自己在Google类似的痛苦经历，特别是在即将获得巨额奖金前被裁，感到不公平。
  
• **裁员的无情现实**：
  - [ivraatiems] 指出裁员让人感到自己对公司的价值微乎其微，无论个人表现多好，裁员可能随时发生。这种现实让人质疑是否值得在工作中付出额外努力。
  - [spicyusername] 强调大公司中员工只是“机器中的齿轮”，高层管理者并不真正关心员工，裁员过程冷酷无情。
  
• **裁员是商业决策，无关个人情感**：
  - [jillesvangurp] 通过自己被Nokia裁员的经历说明，裁员往往是基于商业目标和财务需求，与个人表现无关。他们认为被裁有时反而是个契机，迫使个人重新思考职业方向。
  
• **裁员后的积极转变**：
  - [minraws] 分享了自己被裁后迅速找到更高薪工作，并获得职业成长的经历，鼓励其他人不要因裁员而灰心，可能会有更好的机会。

补充讨论：
• **公司财务表现与裁员的合理性**：
  - [kouteiheika] 质疑公司在创下历史最高收入的情况下仍进行大规模裁员，认为这不合理。
  
• **对员工情感反应的不同看法**：
  - [mont_tag] 和 [h4ckaerman] 认为软件工程师习惯了特权待遇，对裁员反应过度。他们强调裁员是职场常态，员工应更成熟地应对，而不是抱怨或公开批评前雇主。
  
• **职场关系的脆弱性**：
  - [mystifyingpoi] 指出，如果职业关系的终结意味着多年建立的关系也随之结束，那么这些关系可能并不牢固。真正的关系应建立在个人层面，而非公司平台上。
  
• **对职业成就的哲学思考**：
  - [quotemstr] 提供了一种哲学视角，认为在行业中，个人的努力和成就往往是短暂的，但追求卓越本身具有价值，值得个人骄傲。

争议焦点：
- 裁员过程中公司是否应给予员工更多的人情关怀和经济补偿。
- 员工是否应在工作中投入过多的情感和身份认同。
- 裁员决定是否应更多考虑员工的个人表现和贡献。

43658089.article_content:
Table of contents
Goodbye Google, I guess
I can't believe the timing
(386) Comments
Last night, my role at Google was eliminated. I'm quite sick to my stomach, extremely sad, and even more angry.
argyle@google.com
is no more. Just like that.
There's not really anything about this that makes sense.
Goodbye Google, I guess
#
I'm told this comes as a shock to my managers and other Chrome team leaders. I'm told it's not based on merit. I'm told I could find another role.
But I was also immediately ripped away from my calendar, docs, code, and more. Anything nice anyone has to say is immediately met with reality, and reality says "don't let the door hit you on the way out." If I was really welcome to another role, why treat me like a criminal?
I can't believe the timing
#
I was at a Chrome team building offsite, quite literally having some of the most fun and creative innovation with Chrome folks I've had in a while; shoulder to shoulder with incredible engineers, planning ways to make web developers life's easier while raising the quality level of the web.
It's like none of these good moments ever happened.
Like I was never in any of these rooms. Like I wasn't assigned to high priority features or an owner of meaningful work streams.
I was supposed to record a Google IO video next week. A talk I was
very
very excited to give. Gone. Wasted.
I was supposed to be on stage at Google IO, gone.
I was supposed to run a booth right outside the main stage, gone.
I was supposed to help with the developer keynote, ensuring things matched reality and were beautiful. Gone.
CSS Working Group membership, gone.
Developer Office Hours, gone.
Code access to the
Carousel Gallery
, gone.
Helping with Overflow 5, or other CSS work at Google, gone.
Relationships that took me years to cultivate… mostly going to be gone too.
The list of things I was doing is huge. It's going to be a while until I can resume some of them, and many of them won't resume at all.
I feel back stabbed, unappreciated, tossed in the trash. I can't sleep. I'm ashamed. I'm pissed.
I really was just a fuckin cog in a mega corp.
Find me on
Bluesky
or email me at
adam.is@nerdy.dev
if you feel compelled to reach out.
Sorry if I don't reply quickly, it's very overwhelming to read messages about this. The topic is quite sore.

data.title: Darwin's children drew all over the “On the Origin of Species” manuscript (2014)
data.author: arbesman
data.article_summary: 本文简要介绍了达尔文的家庭生活及其子女在其手稿上的涂鸦。文章提到，达尔文的许多作品已被数字化并可通过Darwin Online等网站免费访问，Darwin Manuscripts Project也提供了他的个人笔记和草稿。其中，《物种起源》手稿的少数幸存页中，有一些被达尔文的孩子们涂画，如"水果与蔬菜士兵之战"。这些涂鸦展示了达尔文家庭对自然的观察和艺术天赋。文章还提到达尔文妻子艾玛的日记及其中的涂鸦，显示出家庭的亲密互动。此外，文章简要提及达尔文早逝的女儿安妮，以及家庭为纪念她保存的物品，展现了达尔文一家的深厚情感。文章最后提醒读者，历史名人也有丰富的家庭生活，他们的成就离不开周围人的支持。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：历史上的儿童绘画及相关历史文化背景

不同观点：
• [nkrisc] 认为，通过保存下来的历史儿童绘画（如13世纪的Onfim的桦树皮笔记），可以发现古人与现代人在本质上没有区别。这种观点强调了古今人类共性，有助于更好地理解历史。
• [andrewstuart] 分享了个人经历，提到自己和兄弟小时候被允许在卧室墙上涂画，这种开放的教育方式让他们的童年充满乐趣，且成年后重新粉刷墙壁，没有造成长久影响。
• [behnamoh] 提出相反观点，认为尽管儿童涂鸦行为延续了几个世纪，但在其他方面人类已经发生了巨大变化，百年前的人可能会觉得现代人奇怪且不善交际。

补充讨论：
• [impish9208] 分享了达尔文的结婚优缺点列表，这一趣闻与主题相关但更侧重于个人生活决策，增加了讨论的趣味性。
• [s3r3nity] 提到了莎士比亚第一对开本的装配故事，强调了历史文献中包含的个人笔记和家庭琐事，推荐了一本相关书籍，扩展了讨论的文化维度。
• [Gormo] 质疑文章中未提及查尔斯·巴贝奇与Emma日记的关系，提出了历史人物之间的潜在联系，引发了对历史文献细节的深入思考。
• [cjs_ac] 提到Royal Armouries Ms. I.33文献曾被儿童用作涂色练习，提供了历史中儿童参与文化活动的具体实例。
• [RKFADU_UOFCCLEL] 认为文章提供了一个历史新思维方式的放松时刻，表达了对当前政治紧张局势的反思。
• [casey2] 讨论了相机技术的发展及其对出版物的影响，从达尔文的《物种起源》无照片到后期使用照片，提出了技术进步对文化记录方式的影响。
• [soheil] 和 [neuroelectron] 以幽默方式提及达尔文的进化论及其后代的状况，间接讨论了科学成就与个人生活的对比。
• [anon291] 提出当代社会对育儿的期望和压力，认为现代社会对儿童不友好，并以副总统带孩子参加活动为例，强调了社会变化对家庭生活的冲击。

争议焦点：
• 人类古今行为是否存在本质区别：[nkrisc] 和 [behnamoh] 对此持不同看法，一个强调共性，一个强调现代社会的巨大变化。
• 现代社会对育儿的态度：[anon291] 认为现代社会对儿童不友好，与历史上育儿方式形成对比。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• 历史文献中的个人笔记和家庭琐事如何影响我们对历史的理解（如莎士比亚第一对开本和达尔文的结婚优缺点列表）。
• 技术进步（如相机技术）对文化记录和出版的影响。

43706037.article_content:
Darwin’s Children Drew All Over the
On The Origin of Species
Manuscript (Updated)
By Benjamin Breen –
Published February 12, 2014
Yesterday was Darwin Day, marking the 205th anniversary of the great naturalist’s birth on February 12, 1809. One of the great things about Darwin is that a huge amount of his work is digitized and freely available via sites like
Darwin Online
.
Interested browsers can also check out the
Darwin Manuscripts Project
, a collaborative initiative based at the American Museum of Natural History. Here you can read through Darwin’s personal notes, including gems like his
scratched out book title ideas
. There are also a number of nature drawings that Darwin prepared while writing his masterpiece,
On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection
(1859). Here, for example, is Darwin’s rather skillful drawing of the stamen of a
Strelitizia
flower:
Cambridge University Library DAR 49: 115r
But there are other drawings in Darwin’s papers that defy explanation - until we remember that Darwin and his wife Emma (who, famously, was also his cousin) had a huge family of ten children. Scholars believe that a young Francis Darwin, the naturalist’s third oldest son, drew this on the back of Darwin’s manuscript for
On the Origin of Species
.
“The Battle of the Fruit and Vegetable Soldiers”
Cambridge University Library
Remarkably, this is one of only twenty-eight pages of the manuscript that still exist. The Cambridge University Library has given it the descriptive name “The Battle of the Fruit and Vegetable Soldiers,” and so indeed it seems to be. As near as I can make out, it shows a turbaned soldier mounted on a blueberry squaring off with an English dragoon on a carrot-steed. Perhaps inspired by the 1839-1842 Anglo-Afghan War, and filtered through the Darwin household’s fascination with plants and gardening?
Here’s another drawing from the talented Darwin children, this one seemingly directly inspired by their father’s work. Birds are in the act of catching a spider and a gnat or bee, while flowers and a butterfly appear in remarkable detail. Clearly the family had a knack for acute observations of nature (in fact young Francis ended up becoming a naturalist as well).
Cambridge University Library
This one’s my personal favorite: a child’s-eye view of the Darwin family home with cozy details like a tea kettle on the boil and a fluffy orange cat in the attic window.
Cambridge University Library
Fascinatingly, this image might be detailed enough that it actually depicts Darwin’s famous
sandwalk
, his “thinking path” that led to the family greenhouse (which is, perhaps, the structure visible at the end of the path). The area was later made into a playground for the Darwin children.
I poked around the items available at Darwin Online and came across
Emma Darwin’s diaries
, which are a fascinating resource. Emma seems to have been a talented sketch artist in her own right, doodling profiles and faces in over her daily schedule:
Darwin Heirlooms Trust
Here’s another, perhaps a self-portrait? Write us on
Twitter
or
Facebook
if you have any ideas as to whether this is Emma’s self-portrait or a drawing of another family member.
Darwin Heirlooms Trust
Amazingly, the Darwin kids even got into Emma’s diary, with several pages rendered unreadable by what is almost certainly a crazed toddler’s pencil. In fact, the back page of Emma’s potential self-portrait was defaced in precisely this way:
Francis Darwin strikes again?
Darwin Heirlooms Trust
It’s all a great reminder that even legendary scientists had family lives, and that when we think about history, it’s important to remember that famous figures weren’t working in isolation. They were surrounded by far less famous friends, family members, acquaintances, and enemies. And sometimes, when we get lucky, we see some of their artifacts from the past too.
A tip of the hat, by the way, to
Open Culture
, a website that we’re avid fans of and which wrote the original post about the Darwin kids’ drawings that brought them to our attention. Also be sure to check out
Darwin Online
and the
Darwin Manuscripts Project
, two wonderful resources for anyone interested in the naturalist and his times.
Update:
I also wanted to include a short note on Annie Darwin, who died from tuberculosis at age ten and was Charles’ favorite child (or so he
told
his cousin). This box of items relating to Annie’s life that was collected by Emma Darwin offers another, sadder testimony to the tight-knit dynamic of the Darwin family, and to their artistic knack. Annie’s pink flowers in careful needlepoint seem to echo the exuberant nature drawings of her siblings:
The Darwins’ box of mementos relating to Annie’s life.
American Museum of Natural History
Darwin wrote about Annie after her death with touching earnestness as he tried to set down his memories of her before they faded:
Our poor child, Annie, was born in Gower St on March 2d. 1841. & expired at Malvern at1 Midday on the 23d. of Ap

data.title: Adding keyword parameters to Tcl procs
data.author: BoingBoomTschak
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了在Tcl语言中为`proc`（过程）添加关键字参数（keyword parameters）的功能。作者对某些编程语言缺乏关键字参数以及未向用户提供内置功能感到不满，因此通过几小时的工作，实现了在Tcl中支持关键字参数的方案。文章展示了如何通过包装`proc`来实现这一功能，并给出了具体代码示例，如使用`proc*`定义支持关键字参数的过程，并演示了不同调用方式的结果。此外，作者还比较了使用关键字参数与传统位置参数的性能开销，显示该方法在保持灵活性的同时，性能影响较小。文章最后提到，这种实现借鉴了Tcl中通过强制位置参数来区分选项的特性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Tcl语言中对proc命令增加命名参数功能的各种方案和建议

不同观点：
• [jrapdx3] 支持使用其开发的nxproc扩展来实现Tcl中的命名参数功能。该扩展提供了多种功能，包括常规位置参数、剩余参数、类型检查、对TclOO的支持、以及大小写不敏感的选项。jrapdx3认为nxproc是一个更为全面的解决方案，并且已经提供了跨平台的二进制文件。

• [blacksqr] 建议将OpenACS中的ad_proc工具函数纳入Tcl的内建功能。ad_proc提供了添加开关、内联文档等功能，blacksqr认为将其内置化会非常有用。

• [tracnar] 表示自己曾实现过类似的功能，并认为不需要复杂的quasiquote功能，使用[list {*}$args]即可实现命令的转义。tracnar还提到自己通过包装proc实现了一个pyproc，用于调用Python函数，使其看起来像Tcl的proc。

• [andrewshadura] 认为Tcl作为一种shell已经做得很好，强调其简单、逻辑和一致性，暗示可能没有必要增加复杂的功能。

补充讨论：
• jrapdx3详细介绍了nxproc的功能特点，包括对不同参数类型的支持及其可选的类型检查功能。
• blacksqr强调了ad_proc在OpenACS中的实用性，并认为内置化会带来更多便利。
• tracnar通过自身实践提出了一种更简单的实现方法，并分享了跨语言调用（Tcl和Python）的经验。
• andrewshadura对Tcl的现有设计表示满意，暗示增加复杂功能可能会破坏其简洁性。

争议焦点：是否应该通过扩展或内置功能来增强Tcl的proc命令，以及实现这些功能的最佳方法是什么。jrapdx3和blacksqr提出了不同的扩展方案，而tracnar则认为实现这些功能不需要太复杂。andrewshadura则对增加新功能持保留态度。

Adding keyword parameters to Tcl procs
Published on
2025-04-21
Tags:
tcl
,
programming
Two things that really annoy me with some programming languages: the lack of keyword
(optional, always named and order agnostic) parameters and when the language has a builtin feature
not made available to the user.
Tcl hits the nail here, because a lot of its standard commands have UNIX-like options but
it doesn't make any of this available in either
proc
or
apply
.
But since
proc
can be wrapped "easily" (more later), a few hours gave me
this:
source
.../util.tcl
namespace
path
{::util ::tcl::mathop ::tcl::mathfunc}
proc* p {-flag {-opt foo} x args} {
puts
[lmap v {flag opt x args} {
string
cat
"$v=[set $v]"
}]
}
p 1 a;
# => flag=0 opt=foo x=1 args=a
p -opt bar -flag 1 a;
# => flag=1 opt=bar x=1 args=a
p -flag;
# => flag=0 opt=foo x=-flag args=
#
Relatively constrained overhead
proc
p1
{x} {}
proc* p2 {-flag {-opt foo} x} {}
timerate {p1 1};
# => 0.127049 µs/# 7870986 # 7870986 #/sec 1000.000 net-ms
timerate {p2 1};
# => 0.794317 µs/# 1258943 # 1258943 #/sec 1000.000 net-ms
Pretty nice? As you can see in the third example, I even implemented that Tcl behaviour where
mandatory positional parameter count is used to disambiguate them from options (which is how you
can do
puts $string
without having to safeguard it with a
--
marker).
How it's made

data.title: A new form of verification on Bluesky
data.author: ink_13
data.article_summary: Bluesky推出了一种新的验证系统，以增强用户信任。首先，用户可以将域名设置为用户名以进行验证，目前已有超过27万个账户完成此操作。此外，Bluesky将为真实且重要的账户引入易于识别的蓝色勾标记。同时，推出“可信验证者”功能，允许特定独立组织直接验证账户，这些组织的验证标记为扇形蓝色勾。用户可以查看哪些组织授予了验证，并可选择在设置中隐藏验证标记。目前，用户可以通过设置域名作为用户名进行自验证，暂不接受直接申请验证，但未来将开放申请表。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Bluesky的验证机制及其潜在影响

不同观点：
• **steveklabnik**：对验证机制的技术实现持中立态度。他指出，任何人都可以发布验证记录，但只有被信任的账户会获得蓝标，这类似于技术上的根证书授权（Root CA）。他提到该功能是用户所需求的，并希望该功能能够顺利运行。

• **greyface-**：质疑Bluesky的验证机制与其内部文化愿景（"公司是未来的对手"）是否兼容。他担心如果公司内部出现权力斗争，验证功能可能会像Twitter一样受到影响。

• **gus_massa**：担心验证机制可能被政治实体或不信任的国家用于验证不受欢迎的领导人或大规模验证公民，甚至机器人账户。

• **ajb**：不认同中心化的信任机制，认为这是将信任集中化，而不是反映分布式的社会信任。他主张应由个人决定信任哪些验证者，而不是由Bluesky指定。

• **shrink**：认为使用域名进行身份验证对于非技术人员来说目前不是合适的解决方案，但理解Bluesky选择“信任验证者”的做法是与其价值观一致的。他承认这是一个务实的选择，但不一定是理想的选择。

• **rambambram**：对个人通过自己的网站验证自己并展示蓝标的做法表示怀疑，认为这种做法可能削弱了验证的意义。他更倾向于通过内容本身来判断信息的价值。

• **somat**：认为当前的验证机制优于Twitter的验证，但仍未完全解决问题。他建议跨域验证的解决方案，类似于TLS证书的域验证，但承认一些平台可能不愿意参与这种验证。

• **paxys**：支持信任层级的概念，认为Bluesky验证《纽约时报》，然后《纽约时报》验证其记者，可以使验证过程更具可扩展性。

• **throwawa14223**：认为引入验证机制是反功能的，因为Bluesky的吸引力在于缺乏像Twitter一样的中心化权威。

• **sillysaurusx**：指出许多评论对中心化审核持怀疑态度，但却在一个高度中心化审核的论坛上发表这些评论，认为如果弱审核有积极效果，值得展示。

• **A4ET8a8uTh0_v2**：对验证机制持谨慎乐观态度，认为是大胆的尝试，但担心可能会重蹈覆辙。

• **kristianc**：对验证机制持悲观态度，认为最终可能会导致信任被侵蚀，因为验证标志可能被用于购买地位和冒充他人。

• **FlyingSnake**：认为Bluesky试图回到Elon接手前的Twitter，但可能错失了成为像Signal一样的机会，最终可能只是另一个社交媒体公司。

• **mhh__**：认为旧的蓝标验证机制有助于识别被政权认可的账户，因此对新验证机制持期待态度，尽管他仍在努力适应使用Bluesky。

• **jarjoura**：认为验证机制是限制机器人账户影响力的聪明方式，避免了言论和审查的问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于验证机制是否会导致中心化的信任，以及Bluesky如何在保持去中心化的愿景下有效管理验证过程。
• 验证机制的跨域验证解决方案被认为是更为理想的方式，但实施起来可能面临平台合作的挑战。
• 评论中对中心化审核的态度不一，部分人认为中心化审核在实践中可能具有积极效果，而另一些人则担心其潜在的负面影响。

43753651.article_content:
Trust is everything. Social media has connected us in powerful ways, but it hasn’t always given us the tools to know who we’re interacting with or why we should trust them.
In 2023, we launched our first layer of verification: letting individuals and organizations
set their domain as their username
. Since then, over 270,000 accounts have linked their Bluesky username to their website. Domain handles continue to be an important part of verification on Bluesky. At the same time, we've heard from users that a larger visual signal would be useful in knowing which accounts are authentic.
Now, we’re introducing a new layer — a user-friendly, easily recognizable blue check
. Bluesky will proactively verify authentic and notable accounts and display a blue check next to their names. Additionally,
through our Trusted Verifiers feature, select independent organizations can verify accounts directly
. Bluesky will review these verifications as well to ensure authenticity.
A verified Bluesky account with a blue check.
Trusted Verifiers
Blue checks issued by platforms are just one form of trust. But trust doesn’t come only from the top down; it emerges from relationships, communities, and shared context.
So, we’re also enabling
trusted verifiers
: organizations that can directly issue blue checks. Trusted verifiers are marked by scalloped blue checks, as shown below.
The New York Times account is a trusted verifier with a scalloped blue check.
For example, the New York Times can now issue blue checks to its journalists directly in the app. Bluesky’s moderation team reviews each verification to ensure authenticity.
When you tap on a verified account's blue check, you’ll see which organizations have granted verification.
Tap on the blue check to see which organization verified the user.
You can also choose to hide verification within the app — navigate to Settings > Moderation > Verification Settings to toggle it off.
How to Get Verified on Bluesky
You can self-verify by
setting your domain as your username
. We highly encourage official organizations and individuals to do this.
During this initial phase, Bluesky is not accepting direct applications for verification. As this feature stabilizes, we’ll launch a request form for notable and authentic accounts interested in becoming verified or becoming trusted verifiers.
43753651.article_summary: Bluesky推出了一种新的验证系统，以增强用户信任。首先，用户可以将域名设置为用户名以进行验证，目前已有超过27万个账户完成此操作。此外，Bluesky将为真实且重要的账户引入易于识别的蓝色勾标记。同时，推出“可信验证者”功能，允许特定独立组织直接验证账户，这些组织的验证标记为扇形蓝色勾。用户可以查看哪些组织授予了验证，并可选择在设置中隐藏验证标记。目前，用户可以通过设置域名作为用户名进行自验证，暂不接受直接申请验证，但未来将开放申请表。
43753651.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Bluesky的验证机制及其潜在影响

不同观点：
• **steveklabnik**：对验证机制的技术实现持中立态度。他指出，任何人都可以发布验证记录，但只有被信任的账户会获得蓝标，这类似于技术上的根证书授权（Root CA）。他提到该功能是用户所需求的，并希望该功能能够顺利运行。

• **greyface-**：质疑Bluesky的验证机制与其内部文化愿景（"公司是未来的对手"）是否兼容。他担心如果公司内部出现权力斗争，验证功能可能会像Twitter一样受到影响。

• **gus_massa**：担心验证机制可能被政治实体或不信任的国家用于验证不受欢迎的领导人或大规模验证公民，甚至机器人账户。

• **ajb**：不认同中心化的信任机制，认为这是将信任集中化，而不是反映分布式的社会信任。他主张应由个人决定信任哪些验证者，而不是由Bluesky指定。

• **shrink**：认为使用域名进行身份验证对于非技术人员来说目前不是合适的解决方案，但理解Bluesky选择“信任验证者”的做法是与其价值观一致的。他承认这是一个务实的选择，但不一定是理想的选择。

• **rambambram**：对个人通过自己的网站验证自己并展示蓝标的做法表示怀疑，认为这种做法可能削弱了验证的意义。他更倾向于通过内容本身来判断信息的价值。

• **somat**：认为当前的验证机制优于Twitter的验证，但仍未完全解决问题。他建议跨域验证的解决方案，类似于TLS证书的域验证，但承认一些平台可能不愿意参与这种验证。

• **paxys**：支持信任层级的概念，认为Bluesky验证《纽约时报》，然后《纽约时报》验证其记者，可以使验证过程更具可扩展性。

• **throwawa14223**：认为引入验证机制是反功能的，因为Bluesky的吸引力在于缺乏像Twitter一样的中心化权威。

• **sillysaurusx**：指出许多评论对中心化审核持怀疑态度，但却在一个高度中心化审核的论坛上发表这些评论，认为如果弱审核有积极效果，值得展示。

• **A4ET8a8uTh0_v2**：对验证机制持谨慎乐观态度，认为是大胆的尝试，但担心可能会重蹈覆辙。

• **kristianc**：对验证机制持悲观态度，认为最终可能会导致信任被侵蚀，因为验证标志可能被用于购买地位和冒充他人。

• **FlyingSnake**：认为Bluesky试图回到Elon接手前的Twitter，但可能错失了成为像Signal一样的机会，最终可能只是另一个社交媒体公司。

• **mhh__**：认为旧的蓝标验证机制有助于识别被政权认可的账户，因此对新验证机制持期待态度，尽管他仍在努力适应使用Bluesky。

• **jarjoura**：认为验证机制是限制机器人账户影响力的聪明方式，避免了言论和审查的问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于验证机制是否会导致中心化的信任，以及Bluesky如何在保持去中心化的愿景下有效管理验证过程。
• 验证机制的跨域验证解决方案被认为是更为理想的方式，但实施起来可能面临平台合作的挑战。
• 评论中对中心化审核的态度不一，部分人认为中心化审核在实践中可能具有积极效果，而另一些人则担心其潜在的负面影响。

data.title: Show HN: Dia, an open-weights TTS model for generating realistic dialogue
data.author: toebee
data.article_summary: Dia是由Nari Labs开发的1.6B参数文本到语音（TTS）模型，能够一键生成高度逼真的对话语音。该模型支持基于音频输入控制情感和语气，并能模拟笑声、咳嗽等非语言交流。Dia的预训练模型权重托管在Hugging Face上，并提供与其他模型的对比demo。用户可以通过Gradio UI或命令行工具使用该模型，目前主要支持GPU（PyTorch 2.0+，CUDA 12.6），CPU支持即将添加。Dia初始运行需下载音频编解码器，推理速度取决于GPU性能，完整版需要约10GB显存。该项目遵循Apache-2.0许可证，严禁身份误用、欺骗性内容以及非法或恶意使用。未来计划包括Docker支持、推理速度优化和模型量化。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Dia音频模型的技术成就、应用潜力、开源和许可问题以及技术细节和改进建议

不同观点：
• **技术成就和潜力**：
  - hemloc_io和codingmoh认为，Dia模型展示了当前音频模型领域存在大量低门槛的机会，甚至小团队也能与大公司竞争。
  - xbmcuser和eob认为，Dia模型的出现可能颠覆传统配音和有声书行业，带来全新的音频体验。
  - Versipelle期待Dia模型能够实现从EPUB到有声书的转换，并具备多角色、多语调的生成能力。

• **应用和改进建议**：
  - sarangzambare关注Dia模型在实际应用中的延迟问题，并询问是否支持流式输出。
  - a2128和999900000999询问模型的多语言支持情况，特别是非英语语言的训练和使用。

• **开源和许可问题**：
  - strobe提到Dia模型与GNOME项目的命名冲突，并提供了相关链接。
  - rustc关注Dia项目的许可证类型，并指出项目在使用上的限制，特别是身份误用的禁止条款。

• **技术细节和开发背景**：
  - toebee详细介绍了Dia模型的技术特点和开发背景，包括模型的参数、对话生成方式、音频提示支持等。
  - notdian分享了在M2 Pro MacBook上成功运行Dia模型的经验，并提供了代码链接。
  - noiv提到Dia模型的演示页面在书签功能上的有趣实现。

补充讨论：
- tyrauber对Dia团队提供的音频示例表示赞赏，并希望可以直接分享音频链接。
- vagabund指出Dia模型演示页面的链接问题，但对其音频效果表示肯定。

争议焦点：
- 模型的命名与GNOME项目存在冲突（strobe）。
- 模型的多语言支持和训练过程的透明度（a2128, 999900000999）。
- 许可证中的使用限制，特别是身份误用的问题（rustc）。

Dia is a 1.6B parameter text to speech model created by Nari Labs.
Dia
directly generates highly realistic dialogue from a transcript
. You can condition the output on audio, enabling emotion and tone control. The model can also produce nonverbal communications like laughter, coughing, clearing throat, etc.
To accelerate research, we are providing access to pretrained model checkpoints and inference code. The model weights are hosted on
Hugging Face
.
We also provide a
demo page
comparing our model to
ElevenLabs Studio
and
Sesame CSM-1B
.
Join our
discord server
for community support and access to new features.
Play with a larger version of Dia: generate fun conversations, remix content, and share with friends. 🔮 Join the
waitlist
for early access.
⚡️ Quickstart
This will open a Gradio UI that you can work on.
git clone https://github.com/nari-labs/dia.git
cd
dia
&&
uv run app.py
or if you do not have
uv
pre-installed:
git clone https://github.com/nari-labs/dia.git
cd
dia
python -m venv .venv
source
.venv/bin/activate
pip install uv
uv run app.py
⚙️ Usage
As a Python Library
import
soundfile
as
sf
from
dia
.
model
import
Dia
model
=
Dia
.
from_pretrained
(
"nari-labs/Dia-1.6B"
)
text
=
"[S1] Dia is an open weights text to dialogue model. [S2] You get full control over scripts and voices. [S1] Wow. Amazing. (laughs) [S2] Try it now on Git hub or Hugging Face."
output
=
model
.
generate
(
text
)
sf
.
write
(
"simple.mp3"
,
output
,
44100
)
A pypi package and a working CLI tool will be available soon.
💻 Hardware and Inference Speed
Dia has been tested on only GPUs (pytorch 2.0+, CUDA 12.6). CPU support is to be added soon.
The initial run will take longer as the Descript Audio Codec also needs to be downloaded.
On enterprise GPUs, Dia can generate audio in real-time. On older GPUs, inference time will be slower.
For reference, on a A4000 GPU, Dia rougly generates 40 tokens/s (86 tokens equals 1 second of audio).
torch.compile
will increase speeds for supported GPUs.
The full version of Dia requires around 10GB of VRAM to run. We will be adding a quantized version in the future.
If you don't have hardware available or if you want to play with bigger versions of our models, join the waitlist
here
.

file for details.

This project offers a high-fidelity speech generation model intended solely for research and educational use. The following uses are
strictly forbidden
:
Identity Misuse
: Do not produce audio resembling real individuals without permission.
Deceptive Content
: Do not use this model to generate misleading content (e.g. fake news)
Illegal or Malicious Use
: Do not use this model for activities that are illegal or intended to cause harm.
By using this model, you agree to uphold relevant legal standards and ethical responsibilities. We
are not responsible
for any misuse and firmly oppose any unethical usage of this technology.
🔭 TODO / Future Work
Docker support.
Optimize inference speed.
Add quantization for memory efficiency.
🤝 Contributing
We are a tiny team of 1 full-time and 1 part-time research-engineers. We are extra-welcome to any contributions!
Join our
Discord Server
for discussions.
🤗 Acknowledgements
We thank the
Google TPU Research Cloud program
for providing computation resources.
Our work was heavily inspired by
SoundStorm
,
Parakeet
, and
Descript Audio Codec
.
"Nari" is a pure Korean word for lily.
We thank Jason Y. for providing help with data filtering.

  - **paxys**：应用程序通过制造订单问题，然后仅以账户信用形式“退款”，实际上无法获得现金退款。联系客户支持也非常困难，需要多次沟通才能获得信用卡退款。
  - **ivape**：提到Uber Eats的“买一送一”优惠在购物车中突然改变，导致只收到部分退款，未能考虑机会成本。
  - **JohnMakin**：因误导性的界面被多收了费用，尽管多次联系客户支持仍未解决，最终停止使用该应用。

• **关于订阅取消困难**：
  - **laweijfmvo**：取消订阅可能需要经过多达23个屏幕和32个操作步骤，这种黑暗模式令人抱怨。

  - **janalsncm**：使用虚拟信用卡来管理订阅，如果无法正常取消，则取消信用卡，认为这是一种有效的应对方法。

• **关于企业与监管机构的关系**：
  - **Animats**：提到企业高管通过政治捐款影响政策，暗示监管机构的选择性执法问题。
  - **PicassoCTs**：质疑FTC是否仅在公司未进贡时才“选择性执法”。

• **关于UberOne和竞争对手**：
  - **jonathanlydall**：因UberOne的引入导致配送延迟，转而使用本地竞争对手，认为本地公司配送时间更一致，且资金留在国内更好。
  - **gkapur**：取消UberOne后获得更多折扣，认为UberOne的主要价值在于频繁使用Uber Eats的用户。
  - **creddit**：个人取消UberOne非常容易，且享受了多次免费试用，认为在这方面没有遇到困难。

• **关于市场竞争和价格问题**：
  - **sailfast**：提到Uber通过“钓饵”价格吸引用户选择，但在司机取消后提高价格，认为这种做法令人愤怒。
  - **NoTeslaThrow**：提到出租车被取代后价格上涨，认为这种市场变化对用户和司机都不利，且难以逆转。

- 用户在不同平台上遇到的订阅取消困难和退款问题反映了“黑暗模式”在数字服务中的广泛应用。
- 对UberOne的评价两极化，部分用户认为其对频繁使用者有价值，而另一些用户则因配送延迟和价格问题转向本地竞争对手。
- 企业与监管机构的关系以及政治捐款对政策的影响引发对选择性执法的担忧。
- 使用虚拟信用卡作为应对订阅取消困难的实际解决方案，值得关注。

data.title: LLM-powered tools amplify developer capabilities rather than replacing them
data.author: matthewsinclair
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了大型语言模型（LLM）如Claude Code在编程中的实际作用，指出这些工具更像是增强程序员能力的“机械外骨骼”，而非取代人类程序员。作者通过自己使用Claude Code开发两个应用项目的经验说明，AI工具虽然能大幅加速代码编写过程，但仍需要程序员保持高度警觉，指导工具不偏离方向，并做出关键决策。AI减少了实际编写代码的时间成本，但理解业务问题和设计解决方案变得更加重要。程序员需适应快速生成和丢弃代码的新工作方式，同时保持对整体架构的把控。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）在编程中的作用及其对开发者的影响

不同观点：
• skydhash认为，传统的编码过程分为三个阶段：理解业务问题、设计解决方案和编写代码。他强调，编写代码本身是最简单的部分，如果在这部分花费过多时间，通常意味着前两个阶段没有做好。他还指出，现代工具和IDE已经大大简化了手动代码编辑的繁琐工作。

• ttul从自身长期的开发经验出发，认为LLM可以帮助开发者快速掌握不熟悉的语言或框架，特别是在理解如何将概念应用到具体框架中非常有帮助。他建议新开发者专注于软件工程的大局观，利用LLM来实现这一目标。

• scrlk强调，成功利用LLM的开发者将是那些掌握这些工具潜力及其局限性的人，LLM的目标是增强人类的能力，而不是取代人类。他还引用“计算机是思维的自行车”这一比喻，讨论了如果人人都能使用强大工具，竞争优势将如何体现。

• Aperocky指出，经验在使用LLM时仍然非常重要，因为LLM可能会犯一些细微的错误或选择错误的方向，只有经验丰富的开发者才能纠正这些问题。

• strict9同意AI可以提高效率，但对一些关于开发者将被取代的夸张说法持怀疑态度。他指出，虽然AI工具可以使任务更容易和更高效，但目前还没有看到任何AI解决方案能真正取代开发者。

• pjmlp认为，LLM的最终目标是外包编程任务，而不仅仅是辅助工具。未来的开发环境将是由计算机内部的系统来完成编程，而不是来自世界另一端的团队成员。

• antirez提出了三种程序员类别：完全依赖AI代理编写代码的程序员、将LLM作为工具手动编写和检查代码的程序员、拒绝使用AI的程序员。他认为，第二类程序员目前具有真正的优势。

• bcrosby95认为，“如何做”的阶段不仅仅是编写代码，而是事先了解如何实现。如果对实现没有十足把握，可以先编写代码，然后根据结果更新自己的理解。

• alganet用比喻说明了当前对LLM的期望与现实之间的差距，期望是开发者内部的机械套装，现实是开发者背上的马鞍。

• Workaccount2质疑，当世界充满了能够快速编写代码的初级工程师时，究竟需要多少和什么样的代码。未来的软件开发将如何变化，特别是当每个人都能使用某种程度的LLM工具时。

• ivape希望未来的开发工具能够像钢铁侠的机甲一样，提供完全的即时反馈和直观的操作体验，而不仅仅是现有的IDE和复制粘贴功能。

• submeta认为，LLM工具放大了开发者的能力，而不是取代他们。他分享了自己的经验，利用LLM工具可以独自完成一个团队的工作，但仍需要人类来管理和审查结果。

• sheepscreek总结，未来的开发环境将是一个人扮演整个团队的角色，包括团队领导、经理，甚至项目经理。这样的能力可以带来高收入，或者选择过一种小而满足的生活。

• causal对LLM和其代理在长时间内难以执行功能性任务的根本原因感到好奇，认为文章没有深入解释这一点。

补充讨论：
• LLM工具对开发者的影响和潜在竞争优势。
• 经验在使用LLM工具时的重要性。
• LLM工具是否会最终取代开发者或只是增强其能力。
• 未来开发工具的理想形态和操作体验。
• 不同类型程序员对LLM工具的接受和使用方式。

[ED: There’s a lot of talk of replacing human programmers. Sure, some will go, but not all. My views on how this plays out have changed considerably over the last 2 months. 3 out of 5 hats.]
Why LLM-Powered Programming is More Mech Suit Than Artificial Human
Last month, I used Claude Code to build two apps: an MVP for a non-trivial backend agent processing platform and the early workings of a reasonably complex frontend for a B2C SaaS product. Together, these projects generated approximately 30k lines of code (and about the same amount again thrown away over the course of the exercise). The experience taught me something important about AI and software development that contradicts much of the current narrative.
The Mech Suit Programmer
Remember
Ripley’s final showdown with the Xenomorph Queen in
Aliens
? She straps into the Power Loader—an industrial exoskeleton that amplifies her strength and capabilities. The suit doesn’t replace Ripley; it transforms her into something far more powerful than either human or machine alone.
This is exactly how tools like Claude Code work in practice. They’re not replacement programmers; they’re amplifiers of what I can already do. That backend project? It would’ve taken me months the old way. With Claude Code, I knocked out the core in weeks. But let’s be clear - I wasn’t just describing what I wanted and watching magic happen.
Think of Ripley controlling that Power Loader. Claude Code gave me tremendous lifting power while I maintained control of where we were going. I made all the architectural calls, set the quality bar, and kept us on vision. Most importantly, I had to watch - diligently - for it going off the rails. And when it did (which happened regularly), I had to bring it back into line. The AI cranked out implementation details at incredible speed, but the brain behind the operation? Still mine, and constantly engaged.
Vigilance Required
With great power comes great responsibility. You must maintain constant awareness when working with AI coding tools—something I learned through several painful lessons.
Claude Code occasionally made bewildering decisions: changing framework code to make tests pass, commenting out whole sections of code and replacing them with hardcoded values to achieve a passing test rather than fixing the underlying problem, or introducing dependencies that weren’t necessary or appropriate. It has a massive bias for action, so you have to ruthlessly tell it to do less than it wants to do to keep it under control. I even found myself swearing at it from time to time in a weird form of anthropomorphising that I am still not entirely sure I am comfortable with or properly understand.
Much like piloting an A380, the system handles tremendous complexity but requires a human to grab the yoke at critical moments. Modern aircraft can practically fly themselves, but we still need skilled pilots in the cockpit making key decisions. Taking your eyes off the process, even briefly, can lead to trouble. In my case, the backend required three complete rewrites because I looked away at crucial junctures, allowing the AI to go down problematic implementation paths that weren’t apparent until much later.
This vigilance requirement creates a fascinating dynamic. While the AI dramatically accelerates certain aspects of development, it demands a different kind of attention from the developer—less focus on writing each line of code, more focus on reviewing, guiding, and maintaining architectural integrity.
The Time Cost of Coding
Working with Claude Code has fundamentally shifted how I think about the economics of programming time. Traditionally, coding involves three distinct “time buckets”:
Why am I doing this?
Understanding the business problem and value
What do I need to do?
Designing the solution conceptually
How am I going to do it?
Actually
writing
the code
For decades, that last bucket consumed enormous amounts of our time. We’d spend hours, days or weeks writing, debugging, and refining. With Claude, that time cost has plummeted to nearly zero. I can generate thousands of lines of functional code in a sitting—something that is, frankly, mind-blowing.
But here’s the critical insight: the first two buckets haven’t gone anywhere. In fact, they’ve become
more
important than ever. Understanding the intent behind what you’re building and clearly defining what needs to be done are now the primary constraints on development speed.
And there’s a new skill that emerges: wielding the knife. With code generation being essentially free, we need to become much more comfortable with throwing away entire solutions. The sunk cost fallacy hits programmers hard—we hate discarding code we’ve invested in, fearing we might break something important or never get back to a working state.

data.title: Show HN: Light like the Terminal – Meet GTK LLM Chat Front End
data.author: icarito
data.article_summary: GTK LLM Chat 是一个使用 GTK 构建的图形界面应用，用于与大型语言模型（LLM）聊天。其主要功能包括支持多会话独立窗口、集成 python-llm 以兼容多种 LLM 模型、实时流式响应、消息历史自动滚动、Markdown 渲染、键盘快捷键支持（如 Enter 发送消息，Shift+Enter 换行）、包含外部内容（文件、URL 或文本片段）的提示功能、会话重命名和删除、系统托盘快速访问、自定义系统提示、错误消息处理、动态输入区域等。安装需使用 `pipx` 和 `llm`，系统要求包括 Python 3.8 及以上版本、GTK 4.0 和 libadwaita 等库。该项目遵循 GPLv3 开源许可证。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于软件工具的实现语言、功能暴露以及跨平台支持的讨论

GTK LLM Chat
A GTK graphical interface for chatting with Large Language Models (LLMs).
Key Features
Simple and easy-to-use graphical interface built with GTK
Support for multiple conversations in independent windows
Integration with python-llm for chatting with various LLM models
Modern interface using libadwaita
Support for real-time streaming responses
Message history with automatic scrolling
Markdown rendering of the responses
Keyboard shortcuts (Enter to send, Shift+Enter for new line)
Support for fragments:
Include external content (files, URLs, or text snippets) in your prompts.
Conversation Management:
Rename and delete conversations.
Applet Mode:
Run a system tray applet for quick access to recent conversations.
Model Selection:
Choose from different LLM models.
System Prompt:
Set a custom system prompt for each conversation.
Error Handling:
Clear error messages displayed in the chat.
Dynamic Input:
The input area dynamically adjusts its height.
Keyboard Shortcuts:
Enter
: Send message.
Shift+Enter
: New line in the input.
Ctrl+W
: Delete the current conversation.
Installation
pipx install llm               # required by gtk-llm-chat
llm install gtk-chat
System Requirements
llm
Python 3.8 or higher
GTK 4.0
libadwaita
libayatana-appindicator
Usage
Run the application:
llm gtk-applet
or for an individual chat:
llm gtk-chat
With optional arguments:
llm gtk-chat --cid CONVERSATION_ID  # Continue a specific conversation
llm gtk-chat -s "System prompt"  # Set system prompt
llm gtk-chat -m model_name  # Select specific model
llm gtk-chat -c  # Continue last conversation
Development
To set up the development environment:
git clone https://github.com/icarito/gtk-llm-chat.git
cd gtk-llm-chat
python -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate
pip install -e ".[dev]"

The campaign to subvert Africa's internet registry
In ten days, AFRINIC, the continent's internet registry votes in its new board. But one man has been trying to commoditise its resources, and is pushing for a takeover.
ByÂ
Robert Duigan
PublishedÂ
April 15, 2025
A few weeks ago, we were the subject of several cease-and-desist letters, and a lawsuit, for the first version of this article. Due to delays in securing representation, and delays in communication, we were forced to appear in court before we were prepared. In settlement, we agreed to unpublish the initial version without prejudice, leaving open the right to cover the same story in a new form.
This time around, I am writing in a much more dry and clinical style, and ensuring that all factual claims are linked and cited in context, reserving almost all analysis, opinion and speculation until the very last concluding section. This is done merely to avoid confusion about the status of our claims, all of which are linked to sources in context, for which public resources exist. Other claims are backed up by internal sources. We did not err in our assessment of the story below, and the issue is of significant public interest.
Many thanks to those who have reached out to help, and those who have provided information. We now have adequate legal counsel and are confident that we may defend our claims without trouble.
â
In ten days, AFRINIC, an NGO which functions as the internet registry for the African continent, is supposed be holding its regular board elections, but these have been postponed, and await plans from the official receiver who has taken charge of the company. The organisation manages the distribution of IP addresses for the whole African continent, and apportions them to members, rationing what is, for now, a scarce resource to members who pay limited fees at no profit.
The board elections allow a representative from every member organisation (private companies, universities, government bodies) to vote in a governing body. In these elections, a man is contesting for a position on the basis of cancelling its main functions, and privatising the IP addresses, so that they can be sold, rented and traded for profit without regulation.
This man is Chinese citizen Lu Heng.
â
Crash course
IP addresses identify every device connected to the internet, and are vital to its function. There are two protocols - the limited IPv4, and the virtually unlimited IPv6. The world is running out of IPv4 addresses, with the final blocks allocated in 2011. IPv4's 32-bit structure limits it to about 4.3 billion unique addresses, insufficient for todayâs internet demands. The transition to IPv6, with its 128-bit structure offering vastly more addresses, is critical but slow.
Many organizations cling to IPv4 due to compatibility issues, cost, and complexity of upgrading infrastructure. IPv6 adoption is growing slowly, with only 45% adoption globally, and 5% in Africa. Delays in transitioning could lead to a fragmented internet, higher costs for scarce IPv4 addresses, and hindered innovation.
Meanwhile, lucrative trading of IPv4 blocks has emerged, with prices rising as supply dwindles, further complicating access for smaller players. Switching to IPv6 requires careful rationing of IPv4 to allow a buffer zone, and commoditisation would threaten this, and increase scarcity.
Nobody owns IP addresses. They are allocated to members on the basis of registration services agreements (SRAs), wherein users agree to codes of conduct and commit to specific uses, which they must state up front.
This process is managed by the Regional Internet Registries (RIRs). They manage the distribution of Internet number resources (IP address space and Autonomous System Numbers). They include AFRINIC for Africa, The Asia Pacific Network Information Centre (APNIC), the American Registry of Internet Numbers (ARIN), LACNIC, covering South America and the Caribbean, and RIPE NCC for Europe, the Middle East and Central Asia.
Several of these bodies have been approached or targeted in some way by reform campaigns by Lu Heng.
â
What Lu Heng does
Lu Heng is a Chinese citizen who owns Hong Kong based company
Larus
, which rents and âtradesâ the IPs across the globe.
The dwindling supply of IPv4 numbers has stimulated a
lucrative secondary market
for IPv4 addresses, as companies who receive them practically for free (aside from the membership fees to their RIRs, and the occasional service cost) trade them for an average price of around R900 (US$45) each. This is known, in economic terms, as
rentseeking
-
âgrowing one's existing wealth by manipulating the social or political environment without creating new wealthâ
.
In Africa, Lu Heng owns a company called Cloud Innovation, registered in the Seychelles, as a means for gaining access to AFRINIC, which has some of the few remaining free IPv4 bloc

data.title: Tabular Programming: A New Paradigm for Expressive Computing
data.author: dgellow
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了一种名为“表格编程”（Tabular Programming）的新编程范式，灵感来源于m8 Dirtywave音乐序列器。该范式旨在通过一个简约的表格界面来组织代码，每函数限定五个表达式，以促进代码的模块化和可维护性。硬件方面，使用类似Teensy 4.1微控制器，配备小屏幕和八个按钮，无需键盘即可完成编程。

这种设计有以下优点：
1. **减少错误**：通过选择有效选项，避免许多语法错误。
2. **强制分解**：五表达式限制促使函数的细致分解。
3. **明确数据流**：数据流在表格中视觉化。
4. **便携性**：适合随时随地编程。

文中还展示了如何用这种表格编程实现经典的demoscene等离子效果，通过调用初始化和主循环函数来实现效果。这种新范式探索了在硬件约束下如何创造出新的编程环境。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：表格化编程环境及其在硬件限制下的创新潜力

不同观点：
• **lantry** 认为，这种编程环境不仅仅是将编程能力塞进类似Game Boy的设备中，而是从根本上重新思考如何在特定硬件环境下进行编程。这种方法有助于打破日常软件工程中由于过度依赖抽象而无法完全理解系统的局限，从而可能提升创造性表达。

• **hcarvalhoalves** 指出，最初他以为文章讨论的是其他内容，但实际上是将代码结构化为固定大小的表格。他提供了另一个关于表格的思考角度的视频链接，引导读者从不同视角看待表格化编程。

• **hwpythonner** 认为，这种编程方式让他联想到工业控制系统中的梯形图，二者都强调线性、视觉化的逻辑流，尽管应用领域不同。

• **Johnbot** 提到，这让他回想起IBM RPG II编程语言，强调了表格化编程与早期编程语言的相似性。

• **gregschlom** 认为，文章描述的内容类似于汇编语言，具有简洁的结构（标签、操作码、两个操作数、注释），但质疑其可用性，认为这种方法在实际使用中可能不够友好。

• **debugnik** 提出，这种编程环境可以被视为一种通用音乐跟踪器，并好奇这种用户界面是否适用于逻辑编程而非基于堆栈的编程。

• **poulpy123** 认为，这种编程环境可能作为具有少量按键的音乐音序器的脚本语言有一些趣味，但对于常规计算机则难以想象其具体应用场景。

• **turtleyacht** 提到2002年的“面向表格编程”以及相关讨论，提供了一个历史背景和进一步讨论的链接，引导读者了解更多相关信息。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一在于这种表格化编程环境的实际可用性和应用场景。部分评论者（如gregschlom和poulpy123）对其在常规计算机中的实用性表示怀疑，而其他人（如lantry和debugnik）则认为这种方法可能带来新的创造性表达和应用可能性。

• 不同评论者从不同角度提供了对表格化编程的类比和联想，如梯形图（hwpythonner）、RPG II编程语言（Johnbot）和音乐跟踪器（debugnik），这些类比丰富了对该编程环境的理解和讨论。

• 历史背景的引入（turtleyacht）为讨论提供了更多上下文，帮助读者了解表格化编程在更长时间跨度内的发展和讨论。

Tabular Programming: A New Paradigm for Expressive Computing in Constrained Environments
I've been exploring the m8 Dirtywave tracker for a few months now, and it's been a fascinating experience. If you're not familiar with it, the m8 is a portable music sequencer built on the Teensy platform that combines a minimal 8-button interface with a powerful tabular workflow. What makes it special isn't just its portability or its sound capabilities, but how the hardware and interface work together to create an experience that's simultaneously constrained and liberating.
When I'm making music on the m8, I don't feel like I'm fighting with the UI or solving puzzles. It's more like intuitive cooking - mixing ingredients, tasting, adapting, and discovering new flavors along the way. I can lay on my couch, pick it up, and within minutes be immersed in the creative process. No re-learning complicated interfaces, no decision paralysis from too many options - just pure creative flow.
This experience got me thinking about programming environments. Most of our programming tools are designed for desktop workstations with keyboards, mice, and large displays. But what about a programming environment designed specifically for a minimal, portable hardware interface? What would programming look like if it was built around a tabular interface navigated with just a handful of buttons?
The Core Idea
I've been conceptualizing a programming environment built around a tabular interface inspired by the m8. The key insight is that while traditional programming involves typing long streams of text, we could instead organize code into a structured table with each function defined as rows with fixed columns:
NAME: The function identifier
IN: Input parameter specification
EXP1-EXP5: Five expression cells (the core of execution)
OUT: Output specification
At first glance, limiting each function to just five expressions seems incredibly restrictive. But this constraint actually encourages breaking down complex operations into atomic, composable functions - which tends to produce more maintainable code.
The hardware component is just as important as the software model. The target hardware would be deliberately minimal:
Teensy 4.1 microcontroller (same as the m8)
320x240 display
D-pad, A/B, START/SELECT buttons (8 buttons total)
microSD slot and headphone jack
You would navigate the table with the D-pad, edit cells with the A button (which brings up a contextual menu), and run your program with START. No keyboard needed - all programming happens on the device itself through selection rather than typing.
This isn't just about building yet another programming tool - it's about exploring how hardware constraints can lead to new programming paradigms. When you start from the assumption that your interface has just 8 buttons and a small screen, you're forced to rethink fundamental aspects of how programming works.
The current concept is built on a stack-based model similar to Forth, but that's just an implementation detail. The core innovation is the tabular programming model and how it maps to minimal hardware controls.
Some interesting properties emerge from this design:
Error Reduction
: By selecting from valid options, many classes of syntax errors simply cannot happen
Focused Decomposition
: The five-expression limit forces thoughtful function decomposition
Explicit Data Flow
: Data flow between expressions is visually explicit in the table
Portability
: The entire environment is designed for programming on the go, in casual positions
Real-World Examples: Demoscene Effects
To demonstrate that this concept isn't just theoretical, let's explore how a classic demoscene effect - a plasma - would be implemented using this tabular programming model:

43751168.article_summary:
本文介绍了一种名为“表格编程”（Tabular Programming）的新编程范式，灵感来源于m8 Dirtywave音乐序列器。该范式旨在通过一个简约的表格界面来组织代码，每函数限定五个表达式，以促进代码的模块化和可维护性。硬件方面，使用类似Teensy 4.1微控制器，配备小屏幕和八个按钮，无需键盘即可完成编程。

这种设计有以下优点：
1. **减少错误**：通过选择有效选项，避免许多语法错误。
2. **强制分解**：五表达式限制促使函数的细致分解。
3. **明确数据流**：数据流在表格中视觉化。
4. **便携性**：适合随时随地编程。

文中还展示了如何用这种表格编程实现经典的demoscene等离子效果，通过调用初始化和主循环函数来实现效果。这种新范式探索了在硬件约束下如何创造出新的编程环境。
43751168.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：表格化编程环境及其在硬件限制下的创新潜力

不同观点：
• **lantry** 认为，这种编程环境不仅仅是将编程能力塞进类似Game Boy的设备中，而是从根本上重新思考如何在特定硬件环境下进行编程。这种方法有助于打破日常软件工程中由于过度依赖抽象而无法完全理解系统的局限，从而可能提升创造性表达。

• **hcarvalhoalves** 指出，最初他以为文章讨论的是其他内容，但实际上是将代码结构化为固定大小的表格。他提供了另一个关于表格的思考角度的视频链接，引导读者从不同视角看待表格化编程。

• **hwpythonner** 认为，这种编程方式让他联想到工业控制系统中的梯形图，二者都强调线性、视觉化的逻辑流，尽管应用领域不同。

• **Johnbot** 提到，这让他回想起IBM RPG II编程语言，强调了表格化编程与早期编程语言的相似性。

• **gregschlom** 认为，文章描述的内容类似于汇编语言，具有简洁的结构（标签、操作码、两个操作数、注释），但质疑其可用性，认为这种方法在实际使用中可能不够友好。

• **debugnik** 提出，这种编程环境可以被视为一种通用音乐跟踪器，并好奇这种用户界面是否适用于逻辑编程而非基于堆栈的编程。

• **poulpy123** 认为，这种编程环境可能作为具有少量按键的音乐音序器的脚本语言有一些趣味，但对于常规计算机则难以想象其具体应用场景。

• **turtleyacht** 提到2002年的“面向表格编程”以及相关讨论，提供了一个历史背景和进一步讨论的链接，引导读者了解更多相关信息。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一在于这种表格化编程环境的实际可用性和应用场景。部分评论者（如gregschlom和poulpy123）对其在常规计算机中的实用性表示怀疑，而其他人（如lantry和debugnik）则认为这种方法可能带来新的创造性表达和应用可能性。

• 不同评论者从不同角度提供了对表格化编程的类比和联想，如梯形图（hwpythonner）、RPG II编程语言（Johnbot）和音乐跟踪器（debugnik），这些类比丰富了对该编程环境的理解和讨论。

• 历史背景的引入（turtleyacht）为讨论提供了更多上下文，帮助读者了解表格化编程在更长时间跨度内的发展和讨论。

data.title: Decentralizing Schemes
data.author: NotInOurNames
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了去中心化社交媒体的优势与挑战，特别是去中心化方案中出现的不良用户体验问题。作者以Fediverse和Bluesky为例，说明用户在不同实例或客户端之间分享和互动时可能遇到的困难。例如，用户点击链接后可能无法直接在当前会话中评论或互动，或者被重定向到默认客户端而非自己偏好的客户端。此外，作者提到帖子迁移和实例关闭可能导致内容丢失的风险。文章还介绍了URI和URL的基本概念，强调去中心化系统需要更好的URI处理方案以改善用户体验。最终，作者指出解决这些问题对于去中心化网络的可持续性和用户体验至关重要。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同技术方案在去中心化、跨平台交互和数据持久性方面的比较与争议

不同观点：
• [sambroner] 支持基于URI Schema的Fluid Framework/Copilot设计。这种设计通过URI Schema来加载和展示应用内组件（widgets），并支持跨应用的交互和数据连接。优点是灵活性和可扩展性，但存在安全问题。例子包括白板、文本编辑器等组件。

• [janandonly] 认为Nostr协议是解决跨实例交互和内容迁移问题的更好方案。Nostr通过单一的加密身份和去中心化的中继服务器网络，解决了不同实例间无法交互的问题，同时通过内容哈希和公钥保证了内容的便携性和弹性。此外，Nostr链接可以通过URI自动打开用户偏好的客户端，提高了跨设备和应用的用户体验。

• [immibis] 提出BYOND游戏平台的早期去中心化实践，使用类似byond://的URI Schema来启动游戏。这种方法曾被期望用于应用与网页的集成，但随着应用能够在浏览器内运行，这种做法逐渐消失。

• [quantadev] 认为Nostr解决了身份问题，IPFS解决了数据共享问题，但两者没有很好地结合，导致目前的去中心化生态系统存在割裂。同时批评了ActivityPub（如Fediverse、Mastodon）在用户名中嵌入DNS名称的做法，认为这与自由迁移和抗审查性不符。并对Fediverse社区的一些态度提出批评，认为其在抗审查方面表现不佳。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于不同技术方案的优缺点及其实际应用效果，包括URI Schema的灵活性和安全性、Nostr在跨实例交互和内容迁移方面的优势、以及Nostr与IPFS结合的潜在可能性和目前存在的障碍。
• 讨论还涉及去中心化技术在身份验证、数据持久性和抗审查性方面的不同实现方式及其效果。
• 社区对不同技术方案的接受度和实现细节上的分歧也是讨论的重要部分，尤其是对Nostr和IPFS结合的潜在可能性的探讨。

43750439.article_content:
Decentralizing Schemes
Search
I’m a fan of decentralized social media and that’s partly because I enjoy using it. But mostly because
history teaches that decentralization is the best basis for sustainable, resilient online
conversation. (Evidence? Email!) For the purpose of this
essay, let’s assume that you agree with me. Let’s also assume that our online life is still Web-flavored.
I’m going to describe a few unfortunate things that can happen in a decentralized world,
then look at a basic built-in feature of the Web that might make the problems go away.
Let’s start with bad-experience scenarios
Sharing pain
·
Suppose I post a picture to my social-media feed and since Ash follows me, it shows up in their stream. They can favorite
or boost it, but let’s suppose they think their friend Layla might like it too, so they grab the link and drop into their chat window
with Layla, or maybe they send her an email.
By “link” I mean “URL”, and by “URL” I mean “URI” (the distinction will matter in a bit). Here’s what that looks like, first
on the Fediverse:
https://cosocial.ca/@timbray/114361121438267145
And on Bluesky:
https://bsky.app/profile/tbray.org/post/3lmxrkmwz5k2u
Layla sees the link and clicks it or taps it and yay, there’s the picture. She dislikes it and wants to add a negative comment.
On the Fediverse, if it turns out she’s logged onto
CoSocial.ca
like me she’ll have no trouble, she can fire away.  If she’s logged into
another instance (and the Fediverse has thousands) she’s out of luck, even though she’s got a live Fediverse session. She can
paste the URL or just “@timbray” into her search window and that might get her there indirectly if she’s lucky.
This is a bad experience.
On Bluesky, it’ll probably just work. Well, for now. Because while Bluesky is based on the
AT Protocol
(ATproto for short) which is in theory decentralized, at the
moment Ash is logged into the “App View” at
bsky.app
just like I am, because in practice everybody
on Bluesky is.
But in a future where there are multiple ATproto App Views, which is to say when Bluesky becomes as decentralized as the
Fediverse is today, we’re back with the Fediverse problem, because her browser doesn’t know that the URI
identifies an ATproto post that she should be able to boost or like.
Client pain
·
There’s another problem in this scenario. Suppose Layla
was
logged into CoSocial.ca, but she wasn’t using the
default Mastodon client, but rather an alternative such as
Phanpy
or
Elk.zone
. When Layla clicks on that link she won’t be in her fave Fedi client but back in vanilla
Mastodon.
Not a good experience.
Post portability pain
·
Let’s look at the URI for a different Fediverse post of a pretty picture:
https://mastodon.cloud/@timbray/109508984818551909
It’s one of my posts all right, but it’s not from
cosocial.ca
, it’s from
mastodon.cloud
, which was my first home on the Fediverse.  I left it in December 2022 because it
was sold to another company which is sketchy, by which I mean
Lolicon
-friendly.
Whatever I think of whoever’s running
mastodon.cloud
, I have a lot of posts over there, some of which I care
about. For now, they’re still there, but I’m not contributing any money to those guys, nor will I, so if they pull the plug and
vanish I can’t complain. Only if they do, so do all those posts that I cared about back then and still do a bit.
Another bad experience.
URIs and schemes
·
[Anyone who already understands URIs schemes and so on can skip to the next section.]
Let’s look at that Fediverse link again:
https://cosocial.ca/@timbray/114280972142347258
I call it a “URI” because that’s the official name for what it is.
What they look like and how to use them are very thoroughly specified
in several Internet Engineering Task Force publications starting with
RFC3986
. URLs are also URIs, but URIs can do surprising things that
you’ve probably never seen in the world of ordinary URLs.
The crucial thing about both the Fediverse and Bluesky URIs is that they begin with the magic letters “https” followed by a
colon. All URIs
begin with a short string and a colon; the string is called the URI
scheme
.  For each possible scheme, there’s a set of rules
saying how to handle URIs of that flavor. If it’s “https”, then the rules say, using that Fediverse URI as an example, to make
an encrypted connection to the server at
cosocial.ca
and ask it to send you
/@timbray/114280972142347258
. You’ll get some bytes that represent what the URI identifies.
[Yes, I’m oversimplifying. Sorry.]
While most of the URLs you’re ever likely to encounter begin with “https:” there are other schemes. Suppose your email is
“tim@example.com”. Paste
mailto:tim@example.com
into your browser, hit Enter, and see what happens.  This is a URI
whose scheme is “mailto” and it works just fine.
When I tried this just now on my Mac, all three of Safari, Firefox, and Chrome noticed that I use the
Mimestream
mail app and popped that up. Which shows that somewhere in this computer there’s
a notion

data.title: Coding Neon Kernels for the Cortex-A53
data.author: yeko
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者在FOSDEM会议上展示的用于高性能软件定义无线电（SDR）运行时环境qsdr的工作进展，特别是针对Kria KV260板上ARM Cortex-A53处理器的NEON汇编内核实现。作者解释了如何手写汇编实现一个计算核\(y[n] = ax[n] + b\)，并详细讨论了优化该内核的技巧。由于Cortex-A53的指令时序文档不公开，作者通过微基准测试 reverse-engineer 其指令时序。Cortex-A53是一个按序执行且部分双发射的CPU，这意味着优化代码的手动调整可能带来显著性能提升。作者还讨论了NEON寄存器和指令的并行执行特性，如128位NEON操作会占用两个NEON单元，而64位操作可以并行执行。此外，作者指出CPU与L1缓存之间的加载和存储路径宽度不同，加载为64位，存储为128位。这些细节对优化汇编代码至关重要。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：A53核心的性能表现及其编译器优化问题

不同观点：
• 观点一：A53核心并不理想，尤其是编译器对其优化不足。dmitrygr指出，A53核心在编译器优化方面存在问题，特别是在乘法运算时，Android的AOT编译器生成的代码性能较差。
  
  - 支持论据：dmitrygr提到，ChromeOS团队的实习生使用精确周期模型发现，A53在乘法运算时的代码生成存在问题。一个小补丁就能显著提升A53上大多数Android工作负载的性能，且不会影响A57/A72核心的性能。
  
  - 争议点：尽管有性能改进的补丁，但最终并未发布，暗示存在内部政治原因。

补充讨论：
• 技术细节：评论中提到了具体的核心型号（A53、A57、A72）和编译器类型（AOT编译器），以及特定操作（乘法运算）对性能的影响。这表明在技术层面上，不同硬件架构和编译器优化的匹配度对性能有重要影响。

• 内部决策问题：尽管技术上可以实现性能改进，但由于非技术因素（如内部政治），补丁未能发布，这反映了在技术项目中非技术因素可能对最终结果产生重大影响。

43753117.article_content:
Some weeks ago, I
presented at FOSDEM
my work-in-progress high performance SDR runtime
qsdr
. I showed a hand-written NEON assembly implementation of a kernel that computes \(y[n] = ax[n] + b\), which I used as the basic math block for benchmarks on a
Kria KV260
board (which has a quad-core ARM Cortex-A53 at 1.33 GHz). In that talk I glossed over the details of how I implemented this NEON kernel. There are enough tricks and considerations that I could make a full talk just out of explaining how to write this kernel. This will be the topic for this post.
Note:
this post assumes familiarity with the aarch64 assembly syntax, particularly with the way that NEON registers are denoted depending on the context. For example, you should understand that
v0.4s
and
q0
refer to the same 128-bit NEON register, and
v0.2s
and
d0
denote the 64 LSBs of this same NEON register. It might be worth to review the syntax if this doesn’t make sense immediately to you.
Cortex-A53 characteristics
Something peculiar about the Cortex-A53 is that documentation explaining its instructing timing is not publicly available. There is, for instance, a
Cortex-A57 Software Optimization Guide
, but the equivalent document for the Cortex-A53 is not available. I believe that it exists, but it is only available under an NDA. Therefore, all the wisdom about how to optimize code for the Cortex-A53 is folklore coming from people that have either reverse-engineered instruction timings by performing micro-benchmarks, or which have had access to this NDA documentation. Here are some links that I have found quite useful when starting to understand how the Cortex-A53 works and what tricks can be used:
Assembly still matters: Cortex-A53 vs M1
ARM A53 and A55 dual-issue wiki from Tencent ncnn
A thread about A53 dual-issue capabilities in the ARM forums
7-zip benchmarks for the Cortex-A53
Nevertheless, this documentation has not been sufficient to understand fully how this CPU works. I have written many
instruction timing micro-benchmarks
to verify the claims in these links and to test how other combinations of instructions work.
The Cortex-A53 is an in-order execution CPU with partial dual-issue capabilities. This means that machine code is always executed in order, but under some conditions two instructions can be issued in the same clock cycle and executed in parallel. The in-order execution property is quite interesting for my purposes. First, it makes instruction timing much easier to test and understand. Second, it makes the CPU less tolerant to bad code. An out-of-order CPU might outsmart the programmer by reordering code to avoid stalling, but an in-order CPU can show a huge difference between badly ordered code that keeps stalling and properly ordered code that avoids stalls as much as possible. Therefore, the potential benefits of understanding how the CPU works and optimizing the code by hand are much higher for in-order CPUs.
The following diagram refers to the Cortex-A57 rather than the Cortex-A53, but still can be useful for a preliminary understanding of how the A53 works. The A57 is the A53’s big brother (quite literally, since the two were designed to work as pairs in a big.LITTLE system). The A57 is an out-of-order CPU, but it has some commonalities with the A53.
Cortex-A57 execution pipeline, taken from the
Cortex-A57 Software Optimization Guide
In the diagram we can see that the A57 has two execution units for integer arithmetic. This is also true for the A53. It can dual-issue and execute in parallel integer instructions which have no interdependencies, such as
add x0, x0, x0
add x1, x1, x1
(see
the micro-benchmark
).
Of more interest for this post are the two units marked as FP/ASIMD. These are used for floating-point and NEON instructions. There are some subtleties regarding these two units, and in fact they are not completely interchangeable (at least for the A57), but for our purposes the following mental model should be good enough. Each of the two NEON units works on a 64-bit half of a 128-bit NEON register. Executing a NEON instruction that works with a 128-bit register, such as
fadd v0.4s, v0.4s, v0.4s
takes up both NEON units, so no other instruction that uses NEON registers (even for load/store or data movement to/from a GPR) can be executed at the same time. However, generally speaking, two NEON instructions that only access the 64-bit half of independent NEON registers can dual-issue and execute in parallel. For instance, the following two instructions dual-issue and execute a 64-bit add of 2 floats and a 64-bit load in parallel.
fadd v0.2s, v0.2s, v0.2s
ldr d1, [x0]
(see
micro-benchmark
).
Another thing that is very important to understand is the width of the load and store data paths connecting the CPU to the L1d cache. This is documented in the
Arm Cortex-A53 MPCore Processor Technical Reference Manual
. The load data path is 64 bits, while the store data path is 128 bits. This asymmetry is quite interesting, and the fact t

data.title: Experimenting is above all a process
data.author: tobr
data.article_summary: 文章《Experimenting is above all a process》由Rémi Forte于2025年1月4日发表，探讨了实验作为一种过程的核心本质。作者通过案例分析强调，实验不仅仅是结果导向的活动，更是一个持续探索、学习和调整的动态过程。文章详细描述了实验中可能遇到的挑战和不确定性，指出成功实验的关键在于灵活应对变化、积累经验和不断迭代。作者还建议在实验过程中保持开放的心态，接受失败作为学习的一部分，以推动创新和进步。整体而言，文章呼吁重视实验过程本身的价值，而不仅是最终成果。

• 潜在反对观点：虽然未直接引用，但可以推测有人可能认为实验是基于理性分析和计划，而非单纯的本能。这种观点可能强调科学实验需要严谨的规划和逻辑推导，而非仅仅依赖本能。

补充讨论：
• metalman没有提供具体的例子来支持其观点，但其立场很鲜明，强调本能在实验中的首要地位。
• 争议的焦点在于实验的驱动力是内在本能还是外部理性和计划。这反映了关于科学探索中感性与理性因素的深层次讨论。
• 未有其他评论具体回应metalman的观点，因此这里的讨论较为单向，但潜在的不同立场仍然存在。

data.title: Handwriting activates broader brain networks than typing
data.author: onnnon
data.article_summary: 一项发表在《Frontiers in Psychology》的新研究表明，手写在学习中具有不可替代的作用。研究发现，手写相比打字能激活更多且相互连接的大脑区域，尤其在记忆和感官处理相关的区域。手写通过复杂的时空动作刺激大脑，促进视觉、运动和感官输入的整合，而打字主要是重复性按键动作，缺乏这种整合。研究使用高密度脑电图（EEG）对比了手写和打字时的大脑活动，发现手写在大脑中的theta和alpha频段产生了更广泛的连接，这些频段与记忆形成和注意力相关。因此，过度依赖数字工具可能影响学习效果，手写则能独特地促进大脑活动和学习。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：手写与打字对思考、学习和记忆的影响

不同观点：
• 支持手写的观点：
  - [hintymad] 认为手写能够让思维和书写速度同步，从而促进思考，尤其在数学公式书写中更加有效。
  - [sowbug] 提出纸上手写有助于通过“记忆宫殿”效应帮助记忆，记住笔记的位置有助于回忆内容。
  - [kingofheroes] 个人经验表明手写笔记在记忆方面更有效。
  
• 支持打字或质疑手写优越性的观点：
  - [abeppu] 质疑手写是否真的有助于深度思考和错误检查，认为需要更多行为和表现上的证据，提到一项研究未发现手写和打字在单词记忆上有显著差异。
  - [mbrumlow] 认为打字需要的脑力较少，且单指打字无法代表实际打字情况，质疑研究设计的合理性。
  - [NikolaNovak] 强调研究设计不合理，认为应先进行功能性测试，再做脑成像研究。
  - [constantcrying] 强烈质疑脑活动与学习效果之间的关系，认为这些研究没有实际意义和新的见解。
  
• 中立或综合观点：
  - [jakey_2] 认为手写可能激活更多脑区，但也提出记忆效果可能与花费时间有关，而非仅是手写本身。
  - [alganet] 认为手写和打字各有优势，建议综合利用多种方式以最大化脑力活动。

补充讨论：
• 研究设计的争议：
  - 多位评论者（[mbrumlow], [NikolaNovak], [_aavaa_]）指出研究设计存在缺陷，尤其是让参与者仅用单指打字，无法代表实际打字情况，影响了研究结果的可信度。
  
• 个人经验的多样性：
  - 评论中多位用户分享了个人经验，有些人认为手写更有效（[hintymad], [kingofheroes]），而有些人则质疑手写的实际效果（[abeppu], [constantcrying]），显示出个体差异和不同使用场景的影响。

争议的焦点：
• 手写是否真的比打字更能促进深度学习和记忆效果。
• 现有研究的科学性和设计合理性，尤其是关于脑活动与学习效果之间关系的假设。

总体来看，讨论围绕着手写与打字在学习、记忆和思考中的作用，以及现有研究的合理性和实际应用价值。

While keyboards dominate modern classrooms, a new study in
Frontiers in Psychology
suggests handwriting may be irreplaceable when it comes to learning. Researchers found that writing by hand activates far more extensive and interconnected brain networks compared to typing, particularly in regions linked to memory and sensory processing. These findings provide new evidence that handwriting engages the brain in unique ways, raising concerns about the growing reliance on digital tools for education.
As digital tools replace traditional handwriting in classrooms, concerns have arisen about how this shift might impact learning. Typing on a keyboard is often preferred because it enables children to express themselves more quickly and with less physical strain. However, prior research has shown that handwriting is linked to better memory retention, letter recognition, and overall learning outcomes. The fine motor movements involved in handwriting seem to stimulate the brain differently than typing, but the exact neurological mechanisms behind this difference remained unclear.
To investigate, the researchers focused on brain connectivity, which describes how different brain regions work together to accomplish a task. By comparing brain activity during handwriting and typing, the team hoped to uncover whether the physical act of handwriting promotes more extensive brain communication patterns—patterns thought to support learning and memory formation.
“The brain research on handwriting is really a spin-off of our infant brain research in the
NuLab
, our developmental neuroscience laboratory at the Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU), where we show that babies are born with a brain that is ready to learn from day one,” said study author Audrey van der Meer, a professor of neuropsychology.
For their new study, the researchers recruited 40 university students in their early twenties. To ensure consistency, only right-handed participants were included in the analysis, as determined by a standardized handedness assessment. After excluding participants whose data contained artifacts, the final sample consisted of 36 individuals.
Each participant completed two tasks: handwriting and typing. For the handwriting condition, participants used a digital pen to write visually presented words in cursive directly on a touchscreen. For the typing condition, participants typed the same words on a keyboard using only their right index finger. Participants wrote or typed each word repeatedly within a 25-second window while brain activity was recorded. To avoid visual distractions, the words did not appear on the screen during typing.
Brain electrical activity was measured using high-density electroencephalography (EEG), a method that captures rapid changes in brain activity using a net of sensors placed on the scalp. The researchers focused on connectivity, analyzing how strongly different brain regions communicated with each other while participants wrote or typed.
“In our previous studies, critics sometimes mentioned we had tested too few participants,” van der Meer told PsyPost. “This time, we recruited 40 young adults and were able to use the brain data from 36. This is a massive amount of data given that our EEG nets consist of 256 electrodes and can record data at up to 1,000 Hz.”
The results revealed striking differences in brain activity between handwriting and typing. Handwriting activated far more widespread and interconnected brain networks than typing, particularly in the theta (3.5–7.5 Hz) and alpha (8–12.5 Hz) frequency bands. These brain waves, particularly in the lower frequency range, are associated with memory formation, sensory processing, and attention.
The most significant connectivity patterns during handwriting emerged in central and parietal brain regions, which are involved in processing motor control, sensory input, and higher-order cognitive tasks. In contrast, typing produced far less synchronized activity across these areas, indicating that pressing keys involves far less integration of visual, motor, and sensory input than forming letters by hand.
The researchers proposed that handwriting’s benefits arise from the spatiotemporal complexity of the task. Handwriting requires precise coordination of vision, motor commands, and sensory feedback as the brain continuously adjusts finger and hand movements to shape each letter. Typing, on the other hand, relies on repetitive keystrokes that provide minimal motor variation or feedback.
“In our handwriting research, it becomes clear that the brain works differently when writing by hand as opposed to when typing on a keyboard,” van der Meer explained. “Precisely forming letters by hand requires fine motor skills and involves the body and senses to a much larger degree than typing on a keyboard does. As a result, handwriting involves most of the brain, requiring the brain to communicate fast and efficiently between

data.title: A satellite ended up as a ghostly apparition on Google Earth
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: Online sleuths discovered an image on Google Earth showing a satellite over rural North Texas, appearing five times in different colors. This image was captured by a high-resolution Pleiades satellite on November 30, 2024. The satellite resembles a SpaceX Starlink V2 Mini, with a wingspan of about 100 feet. Its multiple appearances in different colors are due to the Pleiades satellite's ability to capture images in various spectral bands. This rare view highlights the challenge of imaging fast-moving objects in low-Earth orbit, which travel at over 17,000 mph. The image offers insights into satellite speed and the increasing use of commercial imaging satellites for space observation, potentially useful for military or corporate purposes.
